full_judgment:
AKM Abdul Hakim J : This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show case as to why the Order dated 4-11-2019 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 514 of 2019 rejecting the application filed by the defendant-petitioners on 26-8-2019 under Order III, rule 1 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for direction upon the plaintiff to appear in person in court for cross-examination by the defendants on that points as specified in the application and the another Order passed on the same date (4-11-2019) rejecting the application filed by the defendant-petitioners under Order VII, rule 11 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure should not be set-aside and or to pass such other further order/orders as this court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. The plaintiff's case, in short, are that mother of the plaintiff, Amena Khanam acquired the suit land through 2 registered kabalas being Nos. 5975 dated 13-7-1961 area 0.3125 acre and 8501 dated 24-9-1987 area 04.50; that thereafter she made an oral gift infavour of her son, the plaintiff on 2-12-2011 measuring an area of 07.625 decimal land in presence of plaintiff's full brothers Khan Gaffar Mohammad, KGM Zahid Hossain and Khan Gaffar Mohammad, Ashraf Mahmud and delivered possession thereof to him before executing unregistered Bonton Nama dated 04-12-2001; that subsequently, in order to avoid any further complications amongst her other sons and daughters, the plaintiff's mother declared heba by a registered a deed being No. 27610 on 14-12-2012 in respect of 04.50 decimal of land out of total area of 0.24 acre from CS and SA plot No. 22, RS plot No. 90 and 03.125 acre land out total 0.36 acre of land of RS plot No. 90/176 i.e. in total 07.625 acre of land from the said two plots and delivered possession, since then the plaintiff has been possessing the said area of land by virtue the said gift. In the plaint it is further stated that his full brother, defendant No. 3 Mahbubur Rahman Khan did not get any land from the suit land which was described in schedule 'Ka' to the plaint in the 'ghoroa aposh bontonnama' dated 4-12-2001; that on 17-12-2012 the plaintiff through his younger brother, Zahid Hossain came to learn that defendant No. 3 appointed defendant No. 2 as his attorney on 12-12-2012 in respect of the 'ka' schedule land, then the plaintiff through his said brother made a search by vender in the Sub-Registrar's Office, Narsingdi and after obtaining the certified copy on 19-12-2012 confirmed that defendant No. 3 appointed defendant No. 2 as his constituted attorney by a registered power of attorney No. 27492 dated 12-12-2012 and the said power of attorney was executed and registered on commission; that thereafter, the plaintiff through his younger brother Zahid Hossain came to know on 18-12-2012 that defendant No. 1 entered into registered Bainanama with defendant No. 3 dated 12-12-2012, then the plaintiff through his younger brother obtained certified copy on 10-1-2013 and confirmed about the registered bainapotro No. 27493 dated 12-12-2012 executed by defendant No. 3 in favour of defendant No. 1; that thereafter through his said brother, the plaintiff came to know on 12-1-2013 that defendant. No. 2 as constituted Attorney of Defendant No. 3 executed and registered Saf-kabala in favour of defendant No. 1; that plaintiff through his younger brother obtained the certified copy of the kabala on 16-1-2013 and confirmed that defendant No. 2 executed and registered a Saf-kabala Deed No 28315 on 23-12-2013; that it apparent from the bainapotro dated 12-12-2012 and Saf-Kabala deed dated 23-12-2012 that defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 3 in collusion with each other fraudulently created the power of attorney and bainapotro on 12-12-2012 and saf-kabala dated 23-12-2012; that defendant No. 3 revoked the power of attorney No. 27492 dated 12-12-2012 executed in favour of Defendant No. 2 by a Deed of Revocation being deed No. 29015 dated 31-12-2012; that Defendant No. 1 on the basis of Family Settlement Deed dated 4-12-2011, a Deed of partition was executed on 21-1-2013 and registered by Deed No. 1508 dated 22-1-2013 between the plaintiff and his brothers Md Mozibur Rahman Khan, Md Mahbubur Rahman Khan (defendant No. 3), Md Badrul Hossain Khan, KGM Ashraf Mahud, KKM Mohammad, Zahid and 4(four) sisters, namely, Rahima Khanam, Fahmida Khanam, Mahfuza Khanam. As per said partition deed plaintiff got 0.11 acre of land including 0.5 acre land of said schedule 'ka'; that elder brother, Mojibur Rahman Khan got 0.6 acre, younger brother Md Zahid Hossain got 0.03 acre in suit plot, in total 0.20 acre, 0.0288 acre was remained as ejmali for Graveyard and road. Defendant No. 3 did not get any property from suit plot; that defendant No. 1 by dint of kabala dated 23-12-2012 did not get possession of suit 'ka' scheduled land and the plaintiff is in possession thereof; that when defendant No. 1 in collaboration with his uncle Dr. Rafiqul Islam Khan and other terrorists of the locality attempted to take forcible possession of the 'ka' schedule land, plaintiff through his Assistant Bench officer, Md Asaduzzaman lodged a GD entry being number 453 dated 8-2-2013 with the Narsingdi Model Police Station and then on the direction of the Officer-in-charge of the Police Station, Sub-Inspector Moqsed Mollah issued a notice on 08-2-2013 asking both the parties to maintain status quo. The plaintiff further, asserted that defendant No. 3 did not get any share in the suit property by virtue of the 'ghoroa bontonnama' dated 4-12-2011 which was acknowledged in the registered bontonnama dated 21-1-2013. Since defendant No. 3 had no right, title, interest and possession in the 'ka' schedule and after 4-12-2011 executing the power of attorney appointing defendant No. 2 on 12-12-2012 authorising her to sell the 'ka' schedule land and the bainapotro in favour of defendant No. 1 and subsequently to execute and register the kabala dated 23-12-2012 was without jurisdiction; that since the activities of defendant No. 3 as stated herein before, created a cloud to the plaintiff's title in the 'ka' scheduled land, he was constrained to file the suit for declaration of title in 'ka' schedule and further declaration that the deeds as described in schedule 'kha' and 'ga' as illegal, void, fraudulent, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiff. 

 5. That when the Title Suit No. 56 of 2013 was pending in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Narsingdi, due to unavoidable circum-stances the defendants was constrained to file a Transfer Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 2015 before the Hon'ble High Court and accordingly the suit was transferred to the Court of District Judge, Dhaka by the judgment and order dated 30-11-2015. Thereafter the learned District Judge, Dhaka transferred the suit to the Fourth Court of Joint District judge, Dhaka and same was registered as Title Suit No. 36 of 2016 but at one stage of the said proceeding the presiding Judge of the said Court felt embarrassed to hear the suit, then the District Judge, Dhaka transferred the suit to the Court of Joint District Judge, Fifth Court, Dhaka, while the suit was registered as Title Suit No. 273 of 2017 and in the said court after conclusion of the trial i.e. examination and cross-examination of the witnesses and hearing argument suit was fixed on 28-4-2019 for delivery of the judgment. At this stage, the plaintiff filed an application before the Court of District Judge, Dhaka on 28-4-2019 under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure for withdrawing the suit from the Fifth Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka and to transfer the same to any other competent Court, Dhaka. In the meantime the Joint District Judge, Fifth Court, Dhaka also felt embarrassed to hear the suit and the learned District Judge, Dhaka again transferred the suit to the Fourth Court of Joint District Judge, 'Dhaka by an administrative order and the said suit was again registered as Title Suit No. 305 of 2019; that again the defendants filed Transfer Miscellaneous Case No. 354 of 2019 before Court of District judge, Dhaka and upon hearing both the parties the learned District Judge, Dhaka transferred the same to the Second Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka and the suit was renumbered as Title Suit No. 514 of 2019. 

 12. Mr JK Paul, the learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that the learned Joint District Judge committed error of law in rejecting the application filed under Order III, rule 1 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure totally fail to conceive the facts and circumstances of the case and the question on which defendants wanted to cross-examine the plaintiff in person has pointed out in the application. He further submits that there is no bar either in the Code of Civil Procedure or in the Evidence Act to give direction to the plaintiff for his personal appearance for cross-examination in the material points involved in suit when plaintiff did not examine himself in support of his case. He finally submits that learned Joint District Judge rejected the application filed under Order VII, rule 11 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure wrongly invoking the Doctrine of Lispendence as envised in section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, as the plaintiff did not deny the fact since his full brother having acquired the suit property has already transferred the same to the plaintiff by executing registered declaration of heba. Therefore, no cause of action is subsisting to proceed with the suit by the plaintiff. 

 13. On the other hand, Mr Mohammad Bakir Uddin Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 submits that the defendant categorically stated in paragraph No. 3 of the application under Order VII; rule 11 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure dated 28-10-2019 (Annexure-A) that defendant No. 1 transferred the suit `Ica' schedule land which he purchased by 'kha' schedule deed being number 28315 dated 23-12-2012 in favour of Md Mujibur Rahman Khan by registered Heba-bil-Eawaj Deed No. 14653 dated 9-10-2019. This statement of the defendants clearly shows that the defendant No. 1 and 2 have no subsisting interest in the suit 'ka' schedule as such learned Joint District Judge did not commit any error of law in passing the impugned judgment and order dated 4-11-2019 and same has not occasioned failure of justice. He has further submitted that the learned Joint District Judge rightly rejected the application dated 26-8-2019 under Order III, rule 1 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure (Annexure F) there is no scope to recall the plaintiff at this belated stage of suit since evidence was closed long before and the suit is now fixed for argument. Moreover, the plaintiff conducted the present suit through his constituted, who deposed in the suit as PW 1 without any objection by the defendants. Thus the learned Joint District Judge correctly found that the defendants filed this application at this belated stage just to delay and disposal of the suit. He has also submitted that at the time of disposing Civil Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 2015, the Hon'ble High Court Division by order dated 30-12-2015 directed the trial court to dispose of the suit within 4(four) months but the defendant adopted dilatory tactics to prolong the delivery of judgment and, as such, the trial court could not pass the judgment of the suit till today. 

 17. Then on the prayer of the defendants-petitioners it was withdrawn from the Court of Joint District Judge, Narsingdi by order of a Division Bench of the Hon'ble High Court Division in Civil Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 2015 dated 30-11-2015 and sent the same to the learned Court of District Judge, Dhaka with a direction to dispose of the suit with 4(four) months. Subsequently, the learned 'District Judge, Dhaka transferred the aforesaid suit to the Court of Joint District Judge, Fourth Court, Dhaka and the same was renumbered as Title Suit No. 36 of 2016 and then it was again transferred to the Court of Joint District Judge, Fifth Court, Dhaka and renumbered as Title Suit No. 273 of 2017 and in this court trial was concluded, argument was made by the parties and then date was fixed for delivery of judgment on 28-4-2019. At this stage, the suit was again transferred from the Court of Joint District Judge, Fifth Court, Dhaka to Joint District Judge, Fourth Court, Dhaka and renumbered as Title Suit No. 305 of 2019, then again it was transferred to the Court of Joint District Judge, Second Court, Dhaka and renumbered as Title Suit No. 514 of 2019 and the learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Dhaka fixed the suit for hearing argument. 

 18. That it appears that after transfer, when the suit was fixed for argument in the Second Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka, the defendants-petitioners filed a misconceived application on 28-6-2019, under Order III, rule 1 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure (Annexure-F) for personal appearance of the plaintiff before the court for cross-examining him on the points stated in the said application. Admittedly, the plaintiff of the instant suit is a sitting Judge of the High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, who filed the instant suit by his constituted attorney, Zahid Hossain on 27-5-2013. 

 20. It also appears that the plaintiff filed the suit through his Constituted Attorney, KGM Zahid Hossain on 27-5-2013 and his attorney was examined as PW1. For conducting the suit the registered Power of Attorney No. 33 dated 17-2-2013 was filed and marked as (Exhibit No. 1). After filing of the suit and even after closing of the evidence of PW1, the defendants did not feel necessity for personal appearance of the plaintiff. Now, the defendant at this belated stage, when the suit was fixed for Argument filed two applications just to delay and drag the suit and to harass the plaintiff. It is for the plaintiff to decide how he will prove his case, whether by adducing evidence by himself or through his constituted Attorney, there is no legal bar in this respect. 

 24. The power of the court to act under Order XVIII, rule 17 are very wide. Thus, it the Court while considering the judgment finds that there is any ambiguity on the face of the record Court can in proper case, recalls witness, ' who had given evidence, for that purpose. But the power under the rule is discretionary and ought to be exercised with the greatest care and only in the most peculiar circumstances. 

 25. In view of the facts and circumstances of this case, it can not be held that by making the impugned order by the learned Joint District Judge rejecting an application under Order III, rule 1 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure there has been a failure of justice, as such no interference is called for. 

 26. It is worthy to note after conclusion of trial, the learned Joint District Judge, Fifth Court, Dhaka fixed the suit for judgment long before on 28-4-2019. So, the learned Joint District Judge, Second Court can easily dispose of the suit on consideration and appreciation of the evidence and materials on record. Moreover, in the facts and circumstances of the present case, it is apparent the defendants unnecessarily filed this misconceived application at this belated stage in the suit for personal appearance of the plaintiff just to harass, humiliate the plaintiff and adopted dilatory tactics to prolong the disposal of the suit. The said application are not dealt with in this Rule. That the plaintiff has every right to file his case though his constituted Attorney and there is no legal bar to file the suit through his attorney and to prove his case either by himself or through his constituted Attorney. 

 28. In the facts and circumstance of the case, it appears that the suit was filed in the year 2013 and the defendant filed the application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 28-10-2019. Generally however, ends of justice is require that power should be exercised at the earliest opportunity not at this belated stage when the suit was once fixed for delivery of judgment on 28-4-2019 and now fixed for argument. 

 29. In this connection we may profitably refer the decision in the case of Knzi Md Shahjahan vs Md Khalitur Rahman Mndbar reported in 54 DLR (AD) 125 wherein their Lordships held: 

 32. Having regard to the facts and circumstance of the case and the decisions cited above, we are of the view that the learned Joint District Judge did not commit any error of law in rejecting the application filed by the defendant-petitioners under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and same has not occasioned failure of justice. 

 35. In the result, the rule is discharged without any order as to costs. 36. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and since the suit is pending for last 7(seven) years, the trial court is directed to dispose of the suit within a period of 3(three) months from the date of receipt of this judgment and order. The learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Dhaka is further directed not to give any adjournment to either parties since the suit was once fixed for delivery of judgment on 28-4-2019. Earlier on 30-12-2015 this Court in disposing Civil Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 2015 directed the trial court to dispose of the suit within 4(four) months.
